cards.text: Jesus has just appointed His twelve apostles up on the mountain. Now He goes home, and once again a crowd gathers around Him. I mean PACKED, friend.

cards.question: The crowd at Jesus' home is so big that He and His disciples can't even do what?

cards.text: Can't even EAT! I've had a line out my bakery door before, but never one so long I couldn't sneak one cookie off the tray. Then word about all this gets around, and somebody decides it's time to step in.

cards.question: Word about the crowd at Jesus' home gets out. Who goes out to take custody of Him?
As they go to take custody of Jesus, His family is saying, "He is out of His mind."

cards.text: Family will do that. One worried phone call and somebody's already in the car with the engine running.
Meanwhile, some scribes have come down from Jerusalem. And they've got their own explanation for how Jesus drives out demons.

cards.question: The scribes from Jerusalem say Jesus drives out demons by whose power?

cards.text: They even say He's possessed by Beelzebul. That's like a firefighter putting out your kitchen fire, and you look him dead in the eye and go, "Mm. Arsonist."

cards.question: Jesus' family and the scribes from Jerusalem are saying the exact same thing about Him.

cards.text: So Jesus calls them together and begins to speak to them in parables. He opens with a question: "How can Satan drive out Satan?"

cards.question: Jesus asks, "How can Satan drive out Satan?" What's He pointing out?

answers.text: Satan would not fight against himself
Satan is too weak to fight anyone
Demons leave on their own over time

cards.text: Then Jesus paints a picture. Imagine a kingdom divided against itself.

cards.question: Jesus says a kingdom divided against itself can still stand if it's strong enough.

cards.text: Same goes for a house: if a house is divided against itself, it cannot stand. Ever try to move a couch with somebody pushing the OTHER way? That couch lives in the doorway now.
Then Jesus turns it to Satan. What if Satan is divided and rises against himself?

cards.question: Jesus says if Satan is divided and rises against himself, he cannot ___, and his end has come.

cards.text: Now a new picture. Somebody wants to get into a strong man's house and steal his possessions, with the strong man right there.

cards.question: Jesus says no one can steal from a strong man's house unless he first does what?

answers.text: Waits for the strong man to leave
Pays off the strong man's servants

cards.question: Jesus says once the strong man is tied up, his house can be plundered.

cards.text: Jesus isn't done. He says, "Truly I tell you, the sons of men will be forgiven all sins and blasphemies, as many as they utter." ALL of them, friend, and that's coming from a stamper who spent years in a junk drawer sure he was past saving.

cards.question: But then Jesus names one kind of blasphemy that will never be forgiven. Blasphemy against whom?
Mark tells us why Jesus gives this warning about blasphemy against the Holy Spirit. Why?

answers.text: They said He has an unclean spirit
They said He broke the Sabbath
They said He spoke against Moses

cards.text: Then Jesus' mother and brothers come and stand outside. They send someone in to call for Him.

A crowd is sitting around Jesus, and someone tells Him His mother and brothers are outside, asking for Him. It's like being in a packed meeting when somebody pokes their head in the door: "Uh, your family's in the lobby."

cards.question: Jesus hears His mother and brothers are outside asking for Him. How does He answer?

answers.text: With a question about His family

cards.text: Jesus replies, "Who are My mother and My brothers?" Then He looks at the people seated in a circle around Him.

cards.question: Looking at the people seated in a circle around Him, Jesus calls them His mother and brothers.
According to Jesus, who is His brother and sister and mother?

answers.text: Whoever does the will of God
Whoever is born into His family
Whoever comes from the land of Israel

cards.text: Chip, Sparkle and the rest made me a Papa, so I know family isn't only about who you came from. And Jesus says whoever does the will of God is His brother and sister and mother. Friend, that's a family worth joining.

findings.problem: The card says Jesus has just appointed His twelve apostles up on the mountain. That fact comes from Mark 3:13-19, outside the passage, but the card cites only Mark 3:20 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: **References.** Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Can't even EAT!", "I've had a line out my bakery door..." and "Then word about all this gets around...". It isn't the opening card, so it can have at most two.

rule.text: **Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.**

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke and tells no part of the passage, even though it cites Mark 3:21. The "one worried phone call" line also suggests the family is worried. The text never says that, and the card doesn't mark it as Papa Dorin's guess.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: Beelzebul shows up here for the first time, and the card never says simply who he is.

rule.text: **New people.** The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences, counting the couch joke. It isn't the opening card, so it can have at most two.

rule.text: **Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.**

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks about "cannot stand" again. That line repeats in Mark 3:24, 25 and 26, and card 4 already asked about it for 3:24. Card 5 also states "it cannot stand" right before this card, so the blank is already given away.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Jesus isn't done.", the quote from 3:28, and the "ALL of them, friend..." line. It's the first card of a stop, not the opening card of the passage, so it can have at most two.

rule.text: **Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.**

findings.problem: The joke compares sins and blasphemies being forgiven to Papa Dorin being stuck in a drawer "sure he was past saving." Being forgiven and being rescued from a drawer aren't the same action, so the comparison doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This last card restates Mark 3:35, which card 9 just asked about and answered. It moves the passage no further, so it works as a recap card.
This story card has three sentences: the Chip and Sparkle line, the restated verse, and "Friend, that's a family worth joining." It isn't the opening card, so it can have at most two.

rule.text: **Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.**
